exercise.name: Lying Flat Hip Raise

reference.title: Lying Flat Hip Raise (male)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (posterior pelvic tilt and lumbar flexion, legs held vertical)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the hips curl up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short pause, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up, brief pause, 2 s down; no kicking
prescription.progression: Longer pause at the top, then the full lying leg hip raise.

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms by your sides palms down, legs straight up over the hips.
Breathe out and curl the hips off the mat, pressing the feet straight up toward the ceiling.
Pause with the low back peeled off the mat; shoulders and head stay relaxed.
Roll the pelvis down slowly, keeping the legs vertical.
Let the pelvis settle, legs still up.

mistakes.mistake: Kicking the legs to throw the hips up
mistakes.fix: Lift with the abdominals; the feet travel straight up, not toward the head.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the legs drop toward the face
mistakes.fix: Keep the legs about vertical so the pelvis does the work.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing through the neck and hands
mistakes.fix: Hands only steady you; keep the head relaxed on the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping fast on the way down
mistakes.fix: Take about 2 s to roll down.

kinematics.norm: The pelvis curls until the buttocks clear the mat; this curl brings in the lower abdominals (Clark 2003)
About 90 degrees held; the angle eases as the pelvis curls (clinical opinion)
Shoulders and head stay on the mat (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back pain or flexion intolerance: start with a posterior pelvic tilt or the dead bug.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before trunk-flexion work.
modify: Hamstring tightness: bend the knees a little.
Neck tension: relax the head on the mat.
regressions: Posterior pelvic tilt with feet on the floor.
progressions: Lying leg hip raise on the floor.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the pelvis toward the ribs to lift the hips; pelvic-curl movements raised lower rectus activity (Clark 2003, Sarti 1996).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help curl the pelvis and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help curl the pelvis and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Hold the legs up at vertical (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Hold the legs up at vertical (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Press the arms into the mat to steady the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Press the arms into the mat to steady the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the elbows straight as the hands press down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the elbows straight as the hands press down (clinical opinion).
